snip.t: Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (IHPS) is hypertrophy of the circular muscle of the pylorus, causing partial and then complete gastric outlet obstruction in the first weeks of life.
❖ Diagnosis: Classically, pyloric stenosis has been confirmed by performing a test feed,\nwhere the baby is given a milk feed which initially calms the hungry infant, and allows for\nexamination.
Gastric outlet obstruction: chronic ulcer scarring leads to pyloric stenosis; presents with vomiting of undigested food.

Common surgical patterns: metabolic alkalosis with hypochloraemia and hypokalaemia in pyloric stenosis and persistent vomiting; metabolic acidosis in sepsis, bowel ischaemia and fistulae; respiratory acidosis in post-operative hypoventilation.
